newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BEBETO FINALLY BREAKS HIS DUCK FOR FLAMENGO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BEBETO FINALLY BREAKS HIS DUCK FOR FLAMENGO.

text.p: Brazilian striker Bebeto finally broke his Flamengo duck on Wednesday when he scored his first goal since joining them from Spanish side Deportivo Coruna in July.

Bebeto made his mark in style, chipping a free kick over the defensive wall to score the only goal of the game away to bottom club Bragantino in the Brazilian championship. The goal sent Bragantino to their sixth consecutive defeat in the competition.
Botafogo striker Tulio, who scored 50 goals in competitive matches last year, grabbed a hat-trick in his team's 4-1 win over Coritiba.
Injury restricted Tulio to a modest nine goals in this year's Rio de Janeiro championship but he now appears to be back to his best, having scored six times in six Brazilian championship matches.
"I'm now back to a goal a game and I'm not going to stop there," he said.
Leaders Sao Paulo lost their unbeaten record when they were beaten 1-0 at home by Guarani despite creating a wealth of chances. They were jeered off the field by their supporters.
"Sao Paulo fans are very demanding, they're used to winning," coach Carlos Alberto Parreira said.
Referee Leo Feldman was pelted with objects hurled from the crowd after awarding Vitoria a controversial penalty, which they converted, in their 2-2 draw away to Portuguesa.
Riot police used their shields to protect him from the rain of missiles as he left the pitch. Television replays later appeared to justify the penalty award.
